findings.who: A filer had a net loss from a Schedule C business, or a partnership or S corporation K-1 loss, in 2022. The software produced no Form 8995 because there was no deduction to claim, so no return of theirs has either form. Some of that qualified loss has not yet offset later QBI.
findings.why_no: The question asks only whether a return included Form 8995 or 8995-A. The help says 'If no return of yours has either form, answer No.' The truthful answer is no.
findings.irs_text: i8995a p. 6, Line 2: 'including prior year loss carryforwards even if the loss was unreported'; Line 6: 'This amount will offset QBI in subsequent tax years regardless of whether it is reported'
findings.fix: Gate on the fact, not the form. Ask: 'Since 2018, did you (or your spouse) have a net loss from a business, farm, rental, partnership, S corporation, or publicly traded partnership, or did any return include Form 8995 or 8995-A?' Then have the tool compute or ask for the carryforward, including amounts never reported.

findings.who: A filer has passive, at-risk, or basis-limited losses (sections 469, 465, 704(d), 1366(d)) from a qualified business that were suspended in 2019–2024. They are freed in 2025, for example when the activity is sold. No earlier return had Form 8995 because the losses were suspended and there was no QBI deduction.
findings.why_no: No 2024 or earlier return included either form, so the truthful answer is no. The freed loss arises this year from an earlier year's event, and a question about past forms does not reach it.
findings.irs_text: i8995 p. 3: 'When losses or deductions previously suspended by other Code provisions are allowed in calculating taxable income, the qualified portion ... is treated as a qualified net loss carryforward from a separate trade or business ... See Line 3.'
findings.fix: Ask separately whether any business, rental, or K-1 loss suspended after 2017 (passive, at-risk, or basis limits) is allowed on the 2025 return. Add its qualified portion to line 3 whatever the answer to the prior-form gate.

findings.who: A filer held a publicly traded partnership (an energy MLP) whose post-2017 losses were suspended under section 469. They sold it in 2025, freeing the losses. No prior return had Form 8995.
findings.why_no: No earlier return had the form, so the truthful answer is no. The tool then sets the REIT/PTP loss line to false and never refuses.
findings.irs_text: i8995 p. 4: 'the qualified portion of the loss or deduction allowed for each PTP is treated as a qualified net loss carryforward from a separate PTP ... See Line 7'; Line 7: 'even if the loss was from a PTP that you no longer hold an interest in'
findings.fix: Ask outside this gate whether the filer (or spouse) has held a publicly traded partnership since 2018 with a K-1 loss, or one sold or disposed of in 2025. Refuse on yes, or route to a computed line 7.

findings.who: A filer whose prior returns were prepared by software or a preparer that attached Form 8995 for MLP (PTP) K-1 income or a PTP loss. The filer thinks of the MLP as a stock-like investment, not a business, and has no real estate funds.
findings.why_no: The question calls it 'the form for the deduction for business income.' The help says it is filed 'for a business or for dividends of real estate funds' and never mentions publicly traded partnerships.
findings.irs_text: i8995 p. 5, Line 17: 'This amount must be carried forward to next year ... regardless of whether the qualified PTP(s) that generated the loss is still in existence.'
findings.fix: Help text: 'It may have been filed for a business, rental, or farm; for a partnership or S corporation K-1; for REIT dividends (Form 1099-DIV box 5, including from mutual funds and ETFs); or for a publicly traded partnership. Check your return for a form numbered 8995 or 8995-A, even if you did not prepare it yourself.'

findings.who: A married couple files jointly for 2025. Before the marriage, the spouse filed separate returns that included Form 8995 with a business loss carryforward. The filer's own returns never had the form.
findings.why_no: The question mentions the spouse, but the help says 'If no return of yours has either form, answer No.' The filer may read that as limited to their own returns.
findings.irs_text: i8995 p. 5, Line 16: 'This is the amount to be carried forward to the next year. This amount will offset QBI in later tax years regardless of whether the trade(s) or business(es) that generated the loss is still in existence.'
findings.fix: Change the help to: 'If no return of yours or, on a joint return, your spouse's (including returns either of you filed before marrying) has either form, answer No.'

findings.who: A filer has not yet filed the 2024 return, or filed it late after starting the 2025 interview. That 2024 return will include Form 8995 with a loss carryforward. No earlier return had the form.
findings.why_no: 'Did your 2024 tax return ... include' is past tense and refers to a filed return. A filer with no 2024 return on file answers no.
findings.irs_text: i8995a p. 6, Line 6: 'The amount reported on this line must be reported in the next tax year on Schedule C (Form 8995-A), line 2, or Form 8995, line 3'
findings.fix: Ask: 'Does or will your 2024 return (filed or not yet filed), or any earlier one, include ...'
